description: We are  team TMT STEEL BARS, competing in NASA Space Apps Challenge! Powered by creativity, grit and a passion for game design, coding, hardware, web development and visual storytelling, we’re ready to build an unforgettable Space Mission Design Game from the ground up.
summary: Orbital Foundry is an interactive 3D space rocket design, customization, and launch simulation game inspired by Spaceflight Simulator. Players start with an engineering budget and fuel reserves, assemble multi-stage rockets from modular 3D components, customize hull colors and liveries, validate thrust-to-weight and aerodynamic stability, launch from a coastal launchpad complex, and navigate into outer space to reach orbital stations and distant planets.
details:
Orbital Foundry — 3D Space Rocket Design & Launch Simulator

Short Overview:
Orbital Foundry is an interactive, browser-based 3D aerospace engineering and spaceflight game where players design custom multi-stage rockets, customize their paint and liveries, test their designs on a launchpad, and fly missions to orbit and distant planets.

1. What does it do and how does it work?

Orbital Foundry combines a 3D vehicle assembly workshop with a real-time flight physics simulator:

  • Step-by-Step Rocket Building: Players assemble rockets from 14 modular 3D parts across six categories—Nose Cones & Crew Capsules, Body & Avionics Rings, Fuel Tanks, Engines, Jettisonable Side Boosters, and Aerodynamic Wings/Fins. Parts can be added from the builder dock or clicked directly in the 3D viewport to highlight, reorder, or remove with a 100% cost refund.
  • Customization & Pre-Flight Engineering: Players name their spacecraft, pick primary/accent colors, and apply procedural hull liveries (stripes, roll checkers, hazard bands, thermal gold foil). Live engineering diagnostics automatically calculate dry/wet mass, total thrust (kN), Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR), stability score, burn time, and pre-launch warnings.
  • Launchpad, Countdown & Flight Simulation: Moving to Launch Complex 39A initiates a T-5 countdown during which umbilical gantry swing arms retract and cryogenic vapor vents. At ignition, players control throttle (0–100%), steer pitch (A/D or touch controls), jettison spent side boosters (Space), switch between four camera angles (Follow, Wide, Nozzle, Orbit), and engage time-warp (1x–10x) in space.
  • Realistic Failure Testing & Space Exploration: Improperly built rockets fail realistically—underpowered builds (TWR < 1.0) stall on the pad, and finless rockets tumble in the atmosphere—triggering a failure debrief explaining how to improve the design. Successful launches ascend through a shifting sky-to-space atmosphere past Earth's curved horizon to reach the Orbital Relay Station, The Moon, Mars, and Jupiter, earning money and fuel rewards across 6 missions.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Learn Aerospace Principles Through Play: Introduces real concepts—Thrust-to-Weight Ratio, aerodynamic drag, center-of-pressure stability, fuel-to-mass ratios, and multi-stage booster separation—in a hands-on, forgiving environment.
  • Zero Installation & Instant Accessibility: Runs directly in any modern web browser on desktop or laptop without downloads, accounts, or heavy game-engine installers.
  • Beginner-Friendly & Never Soft-Locked: Includes starter rocket presets (Scout Mk-I, Selene Explorer, Ares Heavy), optional beginner SAS flight-stabilization assist, full refunds when iterating on parts, and safety-net Space Grants so players can experiment freely.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The goal of Orbital Foundry is to spark curiosity in aerospace engineering, physics, and space exploration—especially for students and beginners who might find traditional orbital simulators intimidating. By turning trial-and-error failure into clear, actionable engineering feedback ("why did my rocket tip over?" or "why was it too heavy to lift off?"), the project encourages iterative problem-solving and STEM literacy in an engaging 3D format.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Languages: TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, and GLSL (custom vertex/fragment shaders).
  • Frameworks & Libraries: React 19, Three.js (WebGL 3D rendering, PBR materials, RoomEnvironment IBL, OrbitControls, LatheGeometry, ExtrudeGeometry, InstancedMesh, and Points particle systems), Tailwind CSS v4, and Lucide React icons.
  • Build & Runtime Tooling: Vite 8, Node.js, and npm.
  • Procedural Audio & Graphics: HTML5 2D Canvas API (for procedural hull paneling, concrete launchpad textures, smoke sprites, and planetary maps) and the browser Web Audio API (for real-time synthesized engine roar, countdown tones, staging clunks, and alert chimes).
  • Storage: Browser localStorage for saving rocket designs, funds, fuel reserves, and mission progress.

5. How is your project creative?

  • 100% Procedural Assets (Zero External Media Files): Every 3D rocket component, planetary surface (Earth clouds, Moon craters, Mars canyons, Jupiter bands & Great Red Spot), hull livery texture, custom GLSL Mach-diamond exhaust plume, Fresnel atmospheric glow, and sound effect is generated mathematically in code.
  • Constructive Failure-Driven Design Loop: Rather than blocking players from launching flawed rockets, Orbital Foundry lets them test flawed builds on the pad, witness the physical consequence (pad stall, atmospheric tumble, or mid-flight fuel depletion), and receive a tailored engineering tip to fix and relaunch.
  • Clean, Unobstructed Cockpit HUD: Collapsible bottom docks keep the central 3D viewport completely clear so players can inspect their rocket craftsmanship and planetary vistas without visual clutter.

6. What factors did our team consider?

  • Usability for Beginners vs. Engineering Depth: Balanced authentic physics variables (TWR, mass depletion, drag, stability) with intuitive controls, starter presets, and an optional SAS flight assist toggle so both newcomers and space-sim fans enjoy playing.
  • Performance Across Hardware & Software WebGL: Implemented automatic software-WebGL detection, zero-garbage-collection math loops, pooled particle buffers, and avoidance of heavy CSS backdrop-filter blurs over the canvas so frame rates stay smooth across laptops and low-GPU environments.
  • Economic Balance & Replayability: Tuned part prices, 100% part-removal refunds, fuel reserves, and progressive mission payouts so players feel rewarded for scaling up from small suborbital hops to heavy planetary missions.
  • Visual Clarity & Accessibility: Paired high-contrast dark obsidian interfaces with tabular monospace telemetry, clear text diagnostics (never relying on color alone), and both keyboard (W/A/S/D, Space) and on-screen button/slider controls.
